questions.prompt: Naive attention with N = 4,096 and 2-byte values: how many MB does writing S once take (one head)?
questions.explanation: 4096² × 2 bytes = 33.55 MB, and the naive version writes and reads S and P.

questions.prompt: Why is naive attention memory-bound even though it's two GEMMs?
options: The N×N score and probability matrices go to DRAM and back, and their traffic dominates
questions.explanation: The N² intermediates, not the GEMMs, set the traffic.

questions.prompt: In tiled attention, what happens to the running output when a new block raises the running max from m to m'?
options: It is multiplied by e^(m − m'), like the running sum
It's divided by the block size
questions.explanation: Both ℓ and o are rescaled to the new max.

questions.prompt: Is FlashAttention-style tiled attention an approximation?
options: No, it computes exactly the same result (up to floating-point rounding)
questions.explanation: Online softmax makes the blockwise computation exact.

questions.prompt: Doubling the query tile size Br in fused attention…
options: Roughly halves the K/V re-reads, at the cost of more on-chip storage
questions.explanation: K and V are re-read once per query tile.
